newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong hurt by Dal-Tile's Q2 difficulties.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong hurt by Dal-Tile's Q2 difficulties.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc said Wednesday its second-quarter earnings should fall below analysts' estimates because of Dal-Tile International Inc's "earning difficulties".
Earlier, ceramic tile maker Dal-Tile said it expects lower-than-expected earnings plus a charge of $16.1 million or $0.29 a share for uncollectible receivables and overstocked inventories.
Armstrong said its share of the $16.1 million charge will be about $5.1 million, or $0.13 a share. It holds a 34.4 percent stake in Dal-Tile.

"This $0.16 per share setback to our second quarter from our minority interest in Dal-Tile is a bitter disappointment, especially since (Dal-Tile) has hit us with earnings difficulties for two quarters in a row," said Armstrong chief executive G.A. Lorch in a statement.
Armstrong bought 37 percent of Dal-Tile in December 1995 when Armstrong's American Olean Tile Co subsidiary merged with the ceramic tile maker.

It bought an additional $25 million of Dal-Tile's stock in two transactions to mitigate the dilution of its stake after Dal-Tile's public offering in August 1996. This brought Armstrong's stake in Dal-Tile to 34.4 percent.
Armstrong's stock traded at 72-5/8 early Wednesday morning, down 1-7/8. Trading in Dal-Tile shares was delayed Wednesday morning, with the last sale at 18-3/16 on Tuesday.
